My AlertsGo Ad-Free

Follow us on:

Bank unions have called a nationwide strike on September 11, followed by the second Saturday and Sunday. SBI and Union Bank have warned customers of possible disruptions to branch services

September 10, 2026 / 11:25 IST

Banks across India are likely to see disruptions from Friday, September 11, as bank employee unions have called a nationwide one-day strike. Since September 12 is the second Saturday and September 13 is Sunday, customers may effectively face three consecutive days when regular branch services are unavailable.

The State Bank of India (SBI) and Union Bank of India have cautioned customers that banking operations could be affected due to the strike.

https://t.co/plEKpTlzCm

— State Bank of India (@TheOfficialSBI) September 9, 2026

The United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) has called the strike on September 11 over several demands, including the implementation of a five-day banking week and concerns over the Performance Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme.

What are bank unions demanding?

Bank unions are demanding a five-day banking week, based on the agreement reached between the Indian Banks’ Association (IBA) and bank unions under the March 8, 2024, settlement and joint note. Under the proposal, Saturdays other than the second and fourth Saturdays would become holidays, while employees would work additional hours from Monday to Friday.

The unions are also opposing the government’s Performance Linked Incentive (PLI) structure for senior bank officers. Under the framework, Scale IV officers and above could receive PLI of up to 365 days of basic pay plus dearness allowance, while officers up to Scale III would have a maximum of 15 days.

Why are banks effectively closed for three days?

The strike is scheduled for Friday, September 11. This will be followed by the second Saturday on September 12 and Sunday on September 13. Therefore, customers who need branch-based services could face a three-day interruption, although the reasons for closure are different.

Not all banking services will stop during this period. Digital banking channels, including internet banking, mobile banking and UPI, are expected to remain available. SBI has specifically advised customers to use digital channels such as internet banking, YONO, mobile banking and UPI, along with ATMs and Automated Deposit and Withdrawal Machines (ADWMs).

What should bank customers do?

Complete urgent branch work today: Customers who need to deposit or withdraw cash at a branch, submit documents, update KYC details, process certain loan-related work or undertake other branch-dependent activities should complete them before September 11.

Use UPI and mobile banking: Routine payments, fund transfers and other digital transactions can be carried out through UPI, mobile banking and internet banking.

Keep enough cash: Customers who expect to need physical cash over the weekend should withdraw it in advance. ATMs are expected to remain available, but customers should not wait until the last minute for cash requirements.

Plan cheque-related transactions: Customers who are depositing or clearing cheques should factor in possible delays because branch operations and related processing could be affected by the strike.

Use banking correspondents/customer service points: SBI has advised customers to use Customer Service Points (CSPs) for certain banking requirements during the strike.

More bank strikes are planned

The September 11 strike is not the only strike announced by bank unions. The union has also planned further strikes for September 28, 29 and 30, followed by a continuous strike from October 26, 2026. However, banks have said they will make arrangements to minimise disruption, but branch-level services could still be affected.

Therefore, customers with time-sensitive banking work should plan their transactions around the announced strike and holiday dates rather than waiting for the next working day.
